title: Reprocessable and damage-reporting crosslinked polyethylene-based materials  via  reactive extrusion
content: In this work, we report the development of a reprocessable and scratch-reporting polyethylene-based polymer network prepared through reactive extrusion, which enables solvent-free network formation in the final crosslinking step. The reporting properties and reprocessability arise from the incorporation of a mechanochromophore isomerization-based molecule that functions both as a stress-sensing probe and as a dynamic crosslinker. The mechanochromophore naphthopyran was selected for this purpose due to its high chemical stability and ease of functionalization. Dynamic crosslinking was achieved via silyl ether exchange chemistry, which enables the introduction of crosslinking units on polyethylene copolymerized with hydroxyethyl methacrylate (PE-HEMA) without requiring chemical modification of the polymer backbone. The synthetic route includes a solvent-free mechanochemical step for the preparation of the mechanophore precursor, while the final crosslinking reaction was performed by solvent-free reactive extrusion.
